name: Bloodhoof the Elder
summary: During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bloodhoof the Elder near the bridge north of Bloodhoof Village. The ancestral spirit offers them a Coin of Ancestry.

sections.title: A Visit from the Ancestors
sections.body: During the Lunar Festival, spirits of heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Elder Bloodhoof appears near the bridge north of Bloodhoof Village. Travelers honor the sacrifices of the past by approaching him. He offers words of encouragement and a Coin of Ancestry.

sections.title: The Bloodhoof Legacy
sections.body: On Mulgore’s ancestral lands, Elder Bloodhoof joins the living tauren tribes to the memory of their forebears. Honoring the dead is central to tauren spiritual life. It keeps the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those walking the plains in harmony.

faq.q: Where can I find Elder Bloodhoof?
faq.answer: Elder Bloodhoof appears near the bridge just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, beneath a beam of celestial light.

faq.q: What is the purpose of seeking out Elder Bloodhoof?
faq.answer: During the Lunar Festival, travelers seek Elder Bloodhoof to honor the ancestors. In return, the spirit offers a Coin of Ancestry and wisdom about neighboring spirits such as Elder Proudhorn.

faq.q: Why is there a beam of light shining down on him?
faq.answer: The beam of light marks Elder Bloodhoof as an ancestral spirit manifested during the Lunar Festival. It symbolizes a sacred link to the skies and the spirits of the past.

faq.q: Can Alliance characters pay homage to Elder Bloodhoof?
faq.answer: The Lunar Festival ancestors honor all mortals who show reverence, whatever their faction. Alliance travelers must tread carefully because Elder Bloodhoof is near the edge of Horde territory.

faq.q: Who is Elder Proudhorn that this elder mentions?
faq.answer: Elder Proudhorn is another ancestral spirit honored during the festival, in Thunder Bluff. Elder Bloodhoof can guide travelers to him.

faq.q: What do the Coins of Ancestry represent?
faq.answer: Coins of Ancestry are tokens of favor from Azeroth’s honored spirits. They show that a traveler has honored the past, and festival celebrants trade them for festive attire, schematics, and celebratory wares.

angles.text: As a tauren, greeting Elder Bloodhoof on your home soil honors your tribe’s legacy and its part in leading your people to a peaceful haven in Mulgore.
As a druid, you honor the Lunar Festival spirits and commune with the elders. This strengthens your bond with the earth and stars.
As a shaman, you commune with manifest ancestors like Elder Bloodhoof, joining the living with ancestral spirits.
As an Alliance traveler, reaching Elder Bloodhoof means crossing hostile Horde plains into the heart of Mulgore.
